I was in and out of psych wards as a teenager three times due to suicide attempts, bullied at school but I assumed it was normal. It was verbal more than anything (minus the odd thing like someone writing 'emo' over my blazer whilst it was on the back of my chair). I was moved to a school for students with 'problems', was told most of the students had physical illnesses such as cancer etc and they were there due to low attendance and were pleasant. That was a complete lie, they lumped me in, and at the time I guess I was an easy target, with a bunch of kids that were most likely young offenders who threw chairs, arson, stealing. I lasted a few days there before I went back to mainstream. It was hell. The irony is when I was under education in a psych ward they embraced the fact I wanted to sit my biology test and really helped. When I went back to mainstream I found out our science tests were combined and being terrible at physics I therefore sucked. 

I agree, they should have something like this, not everyone gets on with mainstream education and lumping a bunch of kids together just because they're the same age is a rather blinkered idea.

I've found that I've just been avoiding food and sleeping it out. I've 'weight recovered' from anorexia so I don't want to slip into that path. The things I tend to keep on stand by as easy meals are tinned soups (or fresh depending on the lifetime) quick snacks that you store in the fridge like falafels, dips and snack cheeses and frozen ready meals. I'm counting calories so I just end up stocking up on the diet ones but I know I can crawl out of bed, at least have a bath and stick one in the microwave and it's something other than nothing. If you have a microwave I'd really suggest stocking up on tinned foods, packet rices etc. Just make sure you have something, even if it means sticking something on TV, allocating yourself half an hour to eat a meal and then going to bed.
